title: Proportional traffic mixer with p95 smoothing and symbolicated sampling reporter
author: Anika Shah
release_notes: Adds a new workload mixer that proportions traffic across workload classes, p95 smoothing for stable alerting, and a symbolicated sampling reporter for richer profiling traces.
description:
Context and motivation: Production traffic mixes at Redwood are multi-modal and shift over short windows (e.g. batch embeddings, streaming chat, low-latency lookups). Existing synthetic runners either replay a fixed sequence or spawn homogeneous fanouts which miss correlation effects and produce noisy percentile signals. This PR introduces a proportional traffic mixer that synthesizes multi-class load according to configurable weights and a p95 smoothing algorithm to reduce false-positive regressions during automated perf sweeps. It also adds a symbolicated sampling reporter that converts periodic sampler stacks into symbol-resolved NDJSON for downstream profiling/UI consumption.

What this PR changes (high level):
- New workload component: bench/mixers/proportional_mixer.go (mixer that accepts a set of workload descriptors and proportions, supports ramp schedules, jitter, and priority-based backpressure).
- New smoothing util: bench/metrics/p95_smoother.go (exponential windowed smoothing targeted at p95/p99 stability; parameters exposed via config).
- Reporter: bench/reporters/symbolicated_sampler_exporter.go that reads periodic raw stack samples, runs local symbolication on Linux/x86 using the embedded symbol cache, and writes compact NDJSON lines for each sample with keys: timestamp, tenant, lean_stack, symbolized_frames.
- CLI: bin/benchctl mixer-run subcommand with new flags --mixer-config, --smoothtime, --symbol-cache-path.
- Test harness updates: bench/testdata/mixer-scenarios.yaml and unit/integration tests exercising proportional mixes and smoothing thresholds.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc linked (see below)
- [x] Unit tests for mixer math and smoothing edge-cases
- [x] Integration test that validates output rates across classes within 2% of target weight
- [x] Basic symbolication tests with a small C++ sample binary
- [x] Perf run demonstrating reduced p95 variance on a synthetic multi-class workload

Design doc / runbook: https://linear.app/redwood/board/ENG-7891/proportional-traffic-mixer-design (design notes, config knobs, recommended baseline weights for common workloads).

How to run locally: 
1) Build benchctl: make -C bench benchctl
2) Start a lightweight runtime simulator: ./benchctl simulator --config bench/testdata/sim-basic.yaml &
3) Run mixer: ./benchctl mixer-run --mixer-config bench/testdata/mixer-scenarios.yaml --smoothtime 30s --symbol-cache-path /tmp/symcache --output ./out/samples.ndjson
4) Use tools/profview to load out/samples.ndjson for flamegraph/stackwalk visualization.

Backward compatibility and safety: Mixer defaults to a conservative schedule (zero burst, 1s minimum inter-arrival) to avoid accidental overload of shared CI infra. Symbolication is disabled by default in hosted CI via an env flag; the exporter falls back to raw stacks if symbols are unavailable. No API changes to the external benchmark artifact formats were made.

Open questions / follow-ups: 
- We currently run symbolication inline; consider offloading to a separate worker to avoid jitter in sampler loops (follow-up ENG-8023).
- Add tenant-aware rate limits in the mixer (to land as a separate PR).

Related work: complements bench/seq-mixer and bench/phase-scheduler projects; inspired by customer traces used in ENG-7764.
